informal_statement: Issue #301 milestone 1: labeling the edges of a triangulated 2D torus by a history's fluxoid data and reading the labels as Regge edge lengths does not give a geometry determined by ZFA closure. The current labeling is finer than the closure class; the axis labeling is constant on closure. The construction is rejected by its pre-registered kill conditions.

approximation_or_regime.name: Fluxoid-labeled Regge toy model
approximation_or_regime.description: Periodic 10x10 lattice, each square split by its diagonal; two-axis twist histories of length <= 8 as walks from the origin; labels from the walk current (A) or the action vector (B); lengths l = l_ref g(|n|) for four monotone g; Euclidean vertex deficits.
approximation_or_regime.validity_limits: 2D Euclidean only, where the Regge action is topological (Gauss-Bonnet). No Lorentzian signature, no refinement limit, no d >= 3.

formal_statement.statement_scope: Smoothing by any kernel commutes with the lattice divergence and preserves div = 0 for returning histories; a closed, count-balanced plaquette history has nonzero circulation, so ZFA is not the face identity; two histories in one closure class carry different currents; the axis labeling vanishes on count-balanced histories. Deficit angles are not formalized.

formal_object.type: link current of a history on a periodic lattice, its smoothing, and a two-plaquette witness

dependencies.audit_baseline: Five new anchors added to QLF_AxiomAudit and the exact-footprint baseline (513 entries).
dependencies.qlf_bridge_axioms: None. Footprints are propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, or none.

interpretation.map: history -> edge labels -> Regge edge lengths -> vertex deficits
interpretation.formal_status: The labeling and smoothing facts are formal; deficits are floating-point numerics.
interpretation.noncircularity_test: Kill conditions K1-K7 and the verdict rule were committed (3d147d4) before fluxoid_regge.py existed. The construction could have passed K3; it did not.

strange_loop.name: fluxoid labels -> Regge geometry -> closure invariant returned
levels: edge labeling on the triangulated torus
Regge edge lengths and vertex deficits
strange_loop.return_level: the closure verdict, through the divergence of the (smoothed) current
strange_loop.conservative_return: The closure verdict returns: div of the current, smoothed or not, is zero exactly for returning histories (div_walkCurrent, smooth_preserves_closure). The geometry does not return the closure class: it is not a class function (current_not_class_function; 143 geometries in the closed class), and the axis labeling that is a class function is constant on closure.
strange_loop.noncircularity_witness: The verdict rule was pre-registered; K3 and K7 failed against a prior that allowed them to pass.
strange_loop.first_order_note: F: QLF_FluxoidRegge anchors. N: fluxoid_regge.py, floating-point deficits at tolerance 1e-9; exact rational smoothing.
strange_loop.defeater: A labeling that is a function of the closure class and varies across closed histories, with a Regge geometry that returns the class.

proof_obligation.domain: two-axis twist histories on the 10x10 torus
proof_obligation.forward_map: walk current -> lengths l_ref g(|n|) -> deficits
proof_obligation.return_map: div of the (smoothed) current -> closure verdict; no map from deficit vector to closure class exists for labelings A or B
proof_obligation.composite_identity_on: the closure verdict only; it fails on closure classes for the geometry
proof_obligation.falsifier: already falsified for labelings A and B; a new labeling must pass K3 and K7

observable.symbol: face obligations, vertex deficits, geometries per closure class
observable.baseline: ZFA => all zero (K1, K2); one geometry per class (K3)
observable.uncertainties: deficits compared at 1e-9; all counts exact

measurement_protocol.design: No empirical measurement. Pre-registered kill conditions K1-K7 in Continuum_Limit.md, run by exhaustive enumeration to length 8.
measurement_protocol.failure_condition: Verdict rule: reject if labeling A fails K3 or K4, unless labeling B passes K3 and K7.

evidence.F: Smoothing commutes with div and preserves closure; ZFA is not the face identity; current is not a class function; axis labels vanish on closure.
evidence.N: fluxoid_regge.py at L=10, lengths <= 8: K1, K2, K3, K7 fail; K4, K5, K6 pass. Flat closed histories are exactly the zero-current ones under all four length maps.

defeaters.formal: A counterexample to the QLF_FluxoidRegge anchors.
defeaters.interpretation: A different complex or labeling might pass; the rejection covers labelings A and B on this complex only.
defeaters.numerical: Deficit zero-tests at 1e-9 could misclassify a near-flat geometry.
defeaters.conceptual: In 2D the Regge action is topological, so no action convergence can be tested here.

G0.reason: Scope, kill conditions and verdict rule stated before the run.

G1.reason: Anchors in QLF_AxiomAudit and the exact-footprint baseline.

G2.reason: No geometry map that is a class function was found.

G3.reason: Return PARTIAL: the closure verdict returns through div; the Regge geometry does not return the closure class.
